author: The Current
description:
The Jayhawks' Gary Louris describes the origins of the song, "Mr. Lincoln"
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

Gary Louris talks about the origins of the song “Mr. Lincoln,” which appears on The Jayhawks’ 2026 album, “Sanctuary Park,” with drummer Tim O’Reagan on lead vocals. The song is told “from the perspective of a musician in the orchestra pit at Ford’s Theater the night [Lincoln] was shot” on April 14, 1865. With its historic setting, the song could be compared to Norman Blake’s song, “Lincoln's Funeral Train (The Sad Journey to Springfield).” In this interview clip with host Diane of The Local Show, Louris traces the song’s beginnings to a co-writing session he had with Emerson Hart (of the band Tonic) in Nashville in 2013. 

Watch and listen to more from Gary Louris in the video above, and find the full session with the Jayhawks — including their performance of “Mr. Lincoln” — here: https://youtu.be/fUAOqqE2v-A

title: Gary Louris talks about the Jayhawks' song, "Mr. Lincoln"

Yard Act's James Smith reflects on what it means to be an artist from Leeds
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

James Smith of Yard Act talks about what it means to be a musician from Leeds (and the Twin Cities, for that matter) compared to the bigger centers of London, New York and Los Angeles. “You’re the underdog by default,” Smith says, “and I think that just gives you a little bit of an outsider outlook on how things work.”

Hear more of what Smith has to say in the video above.

description:
Watch The Jayhawks perform "Mr. Lincoln" in studio
Support The Current: https://support.mpr.org/youtube or hit the Thanks button

Gary Louris is on a mission to prove that a person in their 70s can still produce some of their best work. That’s indeed rare. But so is keeping a band together for 40 years, being credited as pioneer of Americana music, touring with Johnny Cash … the list goes on for Louris and his iconic Minnesota band, The Jayhawks. 

The Local Show’s September Artist of the Month performed three songs in-studio from their 12th album Sanctuary Park. Producer Bob Ezrin (Pink Floyd, Alice Cooper, Peter Gabriel) volunteered to record the LP after Louris called to catch up with the Canadian legend after he renounced his American citizenship, citing his disgruntlement with the country’s extreme political division.
